# Genesis Apocryphon Column 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 2 | **Condition:** Fragmentary; best-preserved early column

---

**2:1** Then I, Lamech, was overcome with fear and I went to my wife Bitenosh [...]

**2:2** [...] and I said to her:

**2:3** Swear to me by the Most High God, by the Lord of Greatness, by the King of all Eternity,

**2:4** [...] the sons of heaven, that you will tell me the whole truth,

**2:5** whether [...] tell me honestly, without any lies.

**2:6** [...] swear to me [...] with no deception [...]

**2:7** [...tell me everything] honestly [...] and without bitterness

**2:8** [...] whether this child was fathered by the Watchers of Heaven

**2:9** [...] or by the holy ones [...] or by the Nephilim

**2:10** [...] tell me everything [...] the full truth [...]

**2:11** Then my wife Bitenosh spoke to me with fierce intensity

**2:12** and [...] she broke into weeping and cried out: My lord! My own brother!

**2:13** Remember the passion between us; the tender moments of our love

**2:14** and how I gasped with pleasure in your embrace.

**2:15** I am telling you the whole truth.

**2:16** [...]

**2:17** [...] then my heart was deeply shaken within me

**2:18** [...] and when my wife Bitenosh saw that my expression had changed

**2:19** [...] she mastered her anger and spoke to me, saying:

**2:20** My lord and my brother, remember our intimacy!

**2:21** I swear to you by the Great Holy One, by the King of Heaven itself

**2:22** [...] that this seed is yours and this pregnancy is from you

**2:23** and you are the one who planted this fruit in me.

**2:24** No stranger did this, no Watcher,

**2:25** none of the sons of heaven.

**2:26** [...] why has your face become so changed and twisted [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 2 contains one of the most emotionally charged scenes in all Second Temple literature. Bitenosh's desperate defense of her fidelity — invoking their shared intimacy and swearing by the highest divine names — reveals a woman caught between her husband's paranoid suspicion and the terrifying reality of the Watchers' presence. The "planting of fruit" metaphor is rendered to capture its procreative meaning.*
